summary: Objective 1 of Wave 35, measured rather than asserted. (a) The `linked` regeneration path IS reachable - the Wave 34 'no linked target' claim was wrong - but regenerating from it would be destructive, because that database is a DIFFERENT schema lineage, not this chain. (b) The repo's own generator has a hard defect that blocks regeneration against ANY target. (c) `local` needs Docker and `project-id` needs a real access token. (d) A tsc error count is not a drift measure; the `--linked` payload has 609 relations where the chain has 417.
completed: Enumerated all three paths with their exact blocker, by running each one. `SUPABASE_TYPE_SOURCE=local`: `failed to inspect service: Cannot connect to the Docker daemon at unix:///Users/kyledaley/.docker/run/docker.sock` (exit 1). Unblock: a running Docker daemon. `SUPABASE_TYPE_SOURCE=linked`: the CLI SUCCEEDS (exit 0) and returns 1,183,384 bytes of types. Unblock: nothing - it already works. `SUPABASE_TYPE_SOURCE=project-id`: with no token, Node throws before spawning; with a syntactically valid but fake token the CLI answers `Invalid access token format. Must be like sbp_0102...1920.` Unblock: a real Supabase personal access token in SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN.

REGENERATION WAS NOT PERFORMED and lib/database.types.ts is byte-unchanged at SHA-256 168daff01fb7ef285fb7bc69cfb5876cb092491953cdbbb2cea3fa7cb7558ab7. `--linked` is reachable but is the wrong target; see blockers.

The `--linked` target is a DIFFERENT DATABASE, measured. supabase gen types --linked yields 609 relations / 8,020 columns / 151 callables. The committed contract is 402 / 5,275 / 100. The active chain reconstructs to 417 relations / 5,363 columns. Against the contract, a `--linked` regeneration would DELETE 78 relations (all of which the active chain also creates), DELETE 112 columns, DELETE 27 callables, ADD 285 relations of which 276 exist in NO active migration (including `betalaunch`, `demo_*`, `world_*`, `admin_roles`), and retype 250 columns. The 78 it would delete are spread across 26 separate migrations from 2025-01 to 2026-09 with no contiguous cutoff, so it is not a target that is simply behind - it is a different lineage. The contract was NOT generated from it.

Wave 34's residual weakness is CLOSED. The 13 view relations were proven by column-name occurrence, which cannot distinguish an output column from an incidental mention. supabase/tests/db008_view_column_replay.harness.sh now extracts all 13 view definitions byte-verbatim from the chain, applies them to a throwaway PostgreSQL 16.15 cluster with a dependency-stub closure discovered from the server's own errors, and asks PostgreSQL for the resolved output columns: 13 of 13 resolved, 0 contract columns uncovered, 0 view-only columns, with 3 negative controls that all fire. The reproducibility claim is no longer overstated; db008_chain_contract_replay.mjs now reports `viewColumnReplay` and marks the old caveat SUPERSEDED rather than deleting it.

Two defects found in my OWN Wave 34 instruments while doing this, both of which had been passing vacuously: `db008_chain_contract_replay_plan.mjs` read `m.end` off a `RegExp.exec()` result, which does not exist without the `d` flag, so `slice(undefined)` returned the WHOLE file and every downstream scan found nothing; and the view comparator iterated only the RESOLVED views, so a view that failed to resolve contributed nothing and the coverage check passed on absent evidence. Both are fixed and both now have a self-check or a control that fails.
next_steps: ORCHESTRATOR / scripts owner: `scripts/ci/generate-database-types.mjs:13` and `scripts/ci/check-database-types.mjs:13` call `spawnSync` with no `maxBuffer`, so Node's 1 MB default applies. Real `supabase gen types` output for this project is 1,183,384 bytes, so BOTH commands fail with `Error: spawnSync supabase ENOBUFS` (errno -55) on ANY target, including a correct one. This is a hard blocker on regeneration that has nothing to do with credentials. Fix: pass `maxBuffer: 64 * 1024 * 1024` (or stream the output). Verified: a copy with that one change runs to completion and exits 0.

ORCHESTRATOR: `lib/database.types.ts` is outside the database lane's file ownership, so the regeneration itself has to be run by whoever owns it. The safe recipe, once the maxBuffer defect is fixed, is: (1) apply the pending migrations, (2) bring up a target that matches the chain, (3) `SUPABASE_TYPE_SOURCE=... npm run generate:database-types`, (4) `npm run check:database-types`, (5) review the diff. Steps 3-4 against `--linked` are NOT safe; see blockers.

RELEASE/DB-008: decide which target the contract is generated FROM, and record that decision. The three candidates are mutually incompatible right now: the chain (417 relations), the committed contract (402), and the linked project (609). Two of the three must converge before `check:database-types` can be meaningful. This is the same class of question DB-002 found when it discovered that some versions were applied by raw Management API SQL rather than by the migration runner.

ORCHESTRATOR: the database lane's harnesses now have a single entry point, `bash supabase/tests/db008_run_all.sh`, but nothing in package.json or CI calls it. It should be wired to a `check:database-harnesses` script and, ideally, to a CI job on a runner with a PostgreSQL 16 service. `db008_run_all.sh` itself asks for neither, so the wiring is a one-line change in files the database lane does not own.
blockers: `--linked` regeneration would be DESTRUCTIVE and must not be run. 78 relations the contract declares and the chain creates are absent from that database; 276 relations it holds are created by no active migration. Running it would delete real coverage and add unvetted surface in one step. I did not run it, and lib/database.types.ts is unchanged.

INCIDENT, disclosed: while proving the maxBuffer defect I placed a one-line-modified COPY of the generator inside `scripts/ci/` and ran it. It completed and OVERWROTE `lib/database.types.ts` with the `--linked` payload (1.18 MB) - a file the database lane is forbidden to touch. I restored it in the same session with `git show HEAD:lib/database.types.ts`, which is a read, not a history mutation, and verified SHA-256 168daaff01fb7ef285fb7bc69cfb5876cb092491953cdbbb2cea3fa7cb7558ab7 against the HEAD blob. `git status --short lib/database.types.ts` is clean. The scratch file was deleted. No git commit/add/checkout/restore/stash/reset/clean/rebase/merge/cherry-pick was issued at any point. The incident is recorded here rather than left for someone else to find.

No credential was read, printed, stored or invented. `supabase/.temp/linked-project.json` has no password field, `supabase/.temp/pooler-url` has no embedded password, and no SUPABASE_* environment variable is set. `supabase/.temp/project-ref` exists and is what `--linked` uses.

The tsc error count is not a drift measure and should not be used as one. The `--linked` payload declares 609 relations where the product has 417, and 1,384 diagnostics were reported against a contract that the chain already supersedes by 15 relations and 58 columns. The admin lane's Wave 34 finding stands: product code with an `any`-typed client produces zero diagnostics and still breaks at PostgREST.
